messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Which way I provided here is suitable (or correct) for spatial simulation of geostatistical applications?
parts:
Hi,

the main difference I see between the two methods is that in the first, you assume the covariate is smooth enough to be represented by values on the mesh nodes and interpolated in-between, and in the second you assume the covariate can vary quickly between neighbouring grid points. (The m.mesh vs x.grid values).
The second method can be modified to have a smooth covariate as well, but since your example is based on a simulated covariate, and different assumptions for that simulation for each case, it's hard to say which approach would be the most appropriate for a specific real case.

Finn
 

On Tue, 16 Mar 2021 at 14:46, ilovegeo...@gmail.com <ilovegeo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi, I want to use INLA+SPDE to simulate the realizations of 2D phenomenon with irregularly-distributed point observations and covariates of raster type. After reading several papers and books related to R-INLA, I figured out two ways for my task, but I have no idea which one is suitable or correct. Please help me to check my code to give a comment on which option should I choose, thank you in advance. Here I use a simulation dataset for illustration.


library(INLA)
set.seed(0)
########## Simulate a dataset #############
n <- 500
coord <- matrix(runif(2*n), nrow=n)

sigma2 <- 0.6
k <- 10
C <- sigma2*exp(-k*as.matrix(dist(coord)))
S <- drop(rnorm(n)%*%chol(C))

x <- runif(n)
beta <- c(0.9, 1.8)
y <- beta[1] + beta[2]*x + S + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)

########### Modeling with INLA ############
# 1.Mesh
m_mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  coord, 
  max.edge=c(1/k, 2/k), 
  cutoff=0.1/k) 

# 2. Projector matrix
m_A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=m_mesh, loc=coord) 

# 3. SPDE model
m_spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=m_mesh, 
                            alpha=1.5) 

# 4. Stack data
stk.est <- inla.stack(tag='est',
                      data=list(response=y),
                      A=list(m_A, 1), 
                      effects=list(
                        s=1:m_spde$n.spde, 
                        data.frame(b0=1, x=x)))

# 5. Fit
formula <- response ~ 0 + b0 + x + f(s, model=m_spde) 
res <- inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stk.est),
            control.predictor=list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.est)))

######## Stochastic simulation on grid #########
# Option 1: Draw posterior samples on the mesh nodes then project #           to grid
n.mesh <- dim(m_A)[2]
x.mesh <- runif(n.mesh) # roughly simulate the covariate at mesh nodes

stk.mesh <- inla.stack(tag = 'mesh',
                       data = list(response = NA),
                       A = list(1, 1),
                       effects = list(
                         s = 1:m_spde$n.spde,
                         data.frame(b0=1, x = x.mesh)))
stk.all <- inla.stack(stk.est, stk.mesh)

res.mesh <- inla(formula, data = inla.stack.data(stk.all),
                 control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.all),compute = TRUE),
                 control.compute = list(config = TRUE))

nbreal = 100
reals <- inla.posterior.sample(n = nbreal, result = res.mesh)

id.pred.mesh <- inla.stack.index(stk.all, 'mesh')$data
pred.nodes <- sapply(reals, function(x) x$latent[id.pred.mesh])

# preject mesh to grid
projgrid <- inla.mesh.projector(m_mesh, xlim = c(0, 1),
                                ylim = c(0, 1), dims = c(200, 200))
Agrid <- projgrid$proj$A

filepath1 = "./Realizations_Opt1/"

for (i in 1:nbreal){
  grid <- drop(Agrid %*% pred.nodes[, i])
  real = matrix(grid, nrow = 200, ncol = 200, byrow = TRUE)
  write.table(real, file=paste(filepath1, as.character(i), ".txt", sep = ""), quote=F,col.name=F,row.names=F)
}

# Option 2: Draw posterior samples directly on the grid nodes
gridcoo <- projgrid$lattice$loc
x.grid <- runif(dim(gridcoo)[1])
stk.grid <- inla.stack(tag = 'grid',
                        data = list(response = NA),
                        A = list(Agrid, 1),
                        effects = list(s = 1:m_spde$n.spde,
                                       data.frame(b0 = 1, x = x.grid))
                      )
stk.all2 <- inla.stack(stk.est, stk.grid)

res.grid <- inla(formula,
                 data = inla.stack.data(stk.all2),
                 control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.all2),compute = TRUE),
                 quantiles = NULL,
                 control.inla = list(strategy = 'adaptive'),
                 control.results = list(return.marginals.random = FALSE,return.marginals.predictor = FALSE),
                 control.mode = list(theta = res$mode$theta,
                                     restart = FALSE),
                 control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

reals2 <- inla.posterior.sample(n = nbreal, result = res.grid)

id.grid.mesh <- inla.stack.index(stk.all2, 'grid')$data
grid.nodes <- sapply(reals2, function(x) x$latent[id.grid.mesh])

filepath2 = "./Realizations_Opt2/"

for (i in 1:nbreal){
  real2 = matrix(grid.nodes[, i], nrow = 200, ncol = 200, byrow = TRUE)
  write.table(real2, file=paste(filepath2, as.character(i), ".txt", sep = ""), 
              quote=F,col.name=F,row.names=F)
}
